newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty lashes Yemen for abusing human rights.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty lashes Yemen for abusing human rights.

text.p: Amnesty International accused Yemen on Thursday of a wide range of rights abuses despite its ratification of major human rights treaties.

"In theory, Yemen has made progress in the field of human rights, ratifying the major human rights treaties," it said in a 52-page report released after in depth talks with the Yemeni government in July 1996.
"In practice, the Yemeni government remains a major violator of the rights protected by these treaties," it said.
It claimed violations ranged from political arbitrary arrest to unlawful executions and "disappearances", as well as discrimination against women.
"The rights of freedom of expression and association are guaranteed by the Yemeni Constitution, but in practice the exercise of these rights is severly curtailed," it said.

"Disappearance amd extrajudicial execution have been used over the years as tools in political struggles, and have affected the lives of hundreds of people. It is a pattern largely perpetuated by the reluctance of successive governments to stamp them out by effective measures of... prevention".

The London-based group alleged torture by security forces of political suspects and prisoners to gain confessions or as punishment, including beatings with cables and sticks, rape, electric shocks and beating on the soles of the feet.
In other cases, people have died allegedly as a result of torture inflicted during their detention, Amnesty said.
"Kentucky Farruj (chicken)" -- suspension from a metal bar inserted between the hands and the knees which are tied together -- and sleep deprivation were listed as other means of torture.

Flogging and amputation, previously limited to the former Yemen Arab Republic (northern Yemen) became applicable to the whole of unified Yemen after the enactment of a new penal code in 1994, it said.
The Republic of Yemen was formed in 1990 by the merger of the conservative north and the Marxist south, ending hundreds of years of separation.
Some opposition members say human rights abuses, especially the southern area, were rife after a brief civil war in 1994.
Yemeni government officials were not available for comment. But officials have in the past dismissed similar claims by international human rights groups.
